 What to look out for at the 2026 MAMAs
 Published : Nov. 20, 2026 - 13:45:48
 Updated : Nov. 20, 2026 - 14:23:08 
 Add The Korea Herald on Google
 Link copied!
 Lee Jung-joo 
Covering K-pop issues, trends
 Subscribe + 
 Cross-generational collaborations, comeback appearances and prize battles to take center stage as 2-day K-pop awards show kicks off
 (CJ ENM) The 2026 MAMA Awards kick off Friday at Kyocera Dome Osaka, bringing together veteran K-pop acts, rising rookies and some of the year’s biggest releases for two days of awards and one-off performances.
 This year’s ceremony, held under the theme “A Music Interstellar," is built around the idea of connecting different generations, genres and forms of art, according to producer CJ ENM.
 The event will be divided into two chapters, with Friday’s event focusing on artist categories and Saturday’s event centered on performances and works.
 Collaborations, bigger performances 
 Cross-generational collaborations will be one of the ceremony’s biggest draws.
 Veteran duo Panic, which resumed activities this year after roughly two decades, will perform alongside a younger generation of artists including Cortis members Martin and Seonghyeon, Woodz, Zerobaseone’s Kim Taerae, Allday Project’s Woochan and Hearts2Hearts’ Yuha. Panic debuted in 1995, the same year Mnet launched.
 Poster for veteran duo Panic's performance with Cortis' Martin and Seonghyeon, Woodz, Zerobaseone's Kim Taerae, Allday Project's Woochan and Hearts2Hearts' Yuha (CJ ENM) CL, returning to the MAMA stage for the first time in 11 years, will team up with The Black Label’s coed group Allday Project for a collaboration titled “Still the Baddest.”
 The appearance coincides with CL’s first solo performance in five years. Her new digital single, “Iconic,” which includes the title track of the same name and the side track “Say It to My Face,” will be released Friday at 6 p.m., the same time the awards ceremony is set to begin.
 Big Bang will take the stage Saturday, marking its first MAMA Awards appearance in 11 years and adding another milestone to the veteran group’s 20th anniversary year. The trio is expected to debut the live performance of its new digital single, set for release Friday afternoon. The song will be the group’s first release in three months following “BiiiG.”
 Big Bang (YG Entertainment) The MAMA Awards are also leaning heavily into collaborations that extend beyond music.
 Big Bang will join forces with characters from “Dooly the Little Dinosaur,” one of Korea’s best-known animated franchises, while Enhypen will present a cinematic performance blending the group’s fantasy-driven universe with the upcoming third installment of the “Dune” film series.
 Contemporary artist Lee Bae, known for his charcoal-based works, is involved in a collaboration combining visual art and music, while organizers have teased a different project involving Google Gemini and technology-driven elements.
 The performances will unfold on a 360-degree stage designed to improve visibility throughout the dome. Artist seating has also been lowered closer to audience eye level, with performance routes extending into audience areas.
 Awards ceremonies are annual events that many K-pop fans look forward to, as several artists use the awards program to showcase performances on a scale beyond regular music broadcasts.
 Le Sserafim (Source Music) Le Sserafim, returning to the awards show for the first time in three years, said on Thursday that it is preparing a performance involving around 70 dancers and staging that had previously been seen only during its second world tour, “Pureflow,” which covered 31 shows across 22 cities in Asia, North America and Europe since July.
 The girl group last appeared at the MAMA Awards in 2023, when it performed “Eve, Psyche & The Bluebeard’s Wife” with dance crew Mannequeen in a large-scale dance performance.
 Rookie boy group Alpha Driven One will take a different approach, teaming up with choreographers Monika and Lip J. The group is expected to reinterpret the concept of its second EP, “Unbreakable: Beast,” through a performance directed by the two dancers, with an emphasis on choreography and cinematic staging.
 This year’s lineup is the largest the MAMA Awards has ever assembled in a single host city. It features rookies, including Alpha Drive One, Cortis, Hearts2Hearts and Rescene, and veteran performers, such as CL, Hwasa and Big Bang.
 Who will take the awards home? 
 Beyond the performances, attention is also centered on the four grand prizes: Artist of the Year, Album of the Year, Song of the Year and Fans’ Choice of the Year.
 BTS, Blackpink, Big Bang, Stray Kids, Enhypen and Aespa are among the nominees for Artist of the Year, while BTS’ “Arirang,” Blackpink’s “Deadline,” Stray Kids’ “This & That” and Enhypen’s “The Sin: Vanish” are among the contenders for Album of the Year.
 Song of the Year will be chosen from the newly introduced Best Song Top 10, a shortlist of 10 tracks chosen based on streaming and download data. Fans’ Choice of the Year, meanwhile, is determined through fan voting.
 Another point to watch will be whether Mnet delivers on its pledge to improve sound quality. Organizers acknowledged during a press premiere last month that audio quality, particularly for broadcast and live-stream audiences, had been a recurring criticism and said they had been testing ways to reduce the differences between the sound inside the venue and that delivered through digital platforms.
 The MAMA Awards on Friday begin at 6 p.m., while the awards ceremony on Saturday will begin at 3 p.m. Both shows will be live streamed globally through Mnet Plus.
